key_insight: Lung-R1 uses a pulmonary knowledge graph to guide LLM reasoning from EMR evidence, aiming to close the gap between medical knowledge recall and case-level diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This could improve structured, record-grounded support for pulmonary diagnostic reasoning in clinical NLP workflows.
method: Built LungKG, a pulmonary knowledge graph with 59,038 nodes, 164,308 edges, 15 entity types, and 112 relation types.
Trained Lung-R1 with KG-constrained reasoning-chain construction and KG-guided reinforcement learning.
Used the graph as both a reusable knowledge resource and a guide for pulmonary diagnostic adaptation.
evidence_signal: In a 20-system evaluation, Lung-R1-14B achieved state-of-the-art results, including an EMR Diagnosis score of 4.3583 and a 0.1476-point gain over the strongest non-Lung-R1 baseline.
watch_item: Performance was reported on benchmark evaluations, so real-world clinical deployment would still require careful validation across diverse hospitals, patients, and documentation styles.
paper_title: Lung-R1: A Knowledge Graph-Guided LLM for Pulmonary Diagnostic Reasoning
